description: Table 1 is a single-panel, image-rendered composition table titled "Chemical compositions of the investigated low-density steels (wt%)". It has seven columns — the header row reads Steel, Mn, Al, C, N, S, Fe — and two data rows, one per investigated steel, labelled LN and HN. The LN steel contains Mn 28.21, Al 9.90, C 0.82, N 0.0025 and S 0.0085, with Fe given as "Bal."; the HN steel contains Mn 28.10, Al 9.95, C 0.81, N 0.1326 and S 0.0093, also with Fe as "Bal.". No units are printed inside the cells; the "(wt%)" basis is asserted only in the caption. The table demonstrates that the two heats are matched in Mn (≈28 wt%), Al (≈10 wt%), C (≈0.8 wt%) and S (≈0.009 wt%), and are designed to differ essentially only in nitrogen — LN at 0.0025 wt% N versus HN at 0.1326 wt% N, roughly a fifty-fold increase. This single-variable nitrogen contrast is the premise of the whole study: any microstructural or mechanical difference subsequently reported between LN and HN (austenite grain size, AlN inclusions, ferrite content, strength, plasticity, toughness) is attributable to nitrogen addition rather than to alloying-base variation. No data beyond the two rows is visible; there are no plots, micrographs or footnotes in the image.

observations.observation: The table has seven columns headed Steel, Mn, Al, C, N, S, Fe, and exactly two data rows labelled LN and HN.
The two steels differ mainly in nitrogen: 0.0025 wt% N in LN versus 0.1326 wt% N in HN, a roughly fifty-fold increase.
Manganese (28.21 vs 28.10), aluminium (9.90 vs 9.95) and carbon (0.82 vs 0.81) contents are nearly identical between LN and HN.
Iron is reported as the balance ('Bal.') for both steels, with no numeric value printed.
No unit appears inside the table cells; the caption states the compositions are given in wt%.
The caption states the table lists the chemical compositions of the investigated low-density steels.
The paper title identifies the alloy system studied as Fe-28Mn-10Al-0.8C low-density steel.
The abstract attributes the property differences to nitrogen content, with AlN identified as the main inclusion, consistent with the LN/HN nitrogen contrast shown in this table.
The table contains no reaction to thermal or mechanical processing; only as-analysed compositions are given.
